title: VACUOUS: the enforcement half of the entry gate is untested - deleting the sea-fill, comprehension or channel-readiness term from MindBreakthroughCondition leaves all 5497 assertions green
source: CONFIRMED BY MUTATION 2026-10-03 in a throwaway copy of the tree, mind_cultivation scope, 22 suites and 10041 assertions green beforehand. Deleting the sea-fill term from breakthrough_condition.gd:25-35: Results: 10041 passed, 0 failed - zero shipped assertions died, and --suite tribulation_once stayed 37 passed, 0 failed. Deleting the comprehension term: Results: 10041 passed, 0 failed. Deleting the channel-readiness term: Results: 10041 passed, 0 failed. Every restore was byte-identical (SHA256 verified). The enforcement itself is real: a purpose-built probe run on pristine code passed 10 of 10 and failed exactly the mutated term, so this is unobserved coverage, not a missing rule. Note the whole-repo number in the old title (5497) is stale; the mind scope alone is 10041 today.
next: Root cause is not a missing assertion, it is what the suite can express. Every place the conjunction is asserted FALSE uses an actor on which ALL gates are shut - test_mind_gate_permissiveness.gd:214 (preview.ready false on a bare actor) and :192 (can_advance false on a bare actor) - so deleting any single term changes nothing. The reachability half asks the opposite question one gate at a time (test_mind_reachability.gd compares value >= required per gate), and Probe.prepared() never stocks the TARGET realm breakthrough pill, so no shipped test ever holds an actor that satisfies everything and can therefore not break exactly one gate. Fix in that order: make prepared() stock the target pill, then add one test per gate that starts from that actor, breaks exactly that clause, and asserts can_advance is false. The unmet states are player-reachable, so no drain is needed - an empty reservoir is reachable by draining the pool directly, comprehension by a tribulation wave toll, and the channel clause by a deviation burning one. Longer term, make preview and MindBreakthroughCondition share one implementation so the two lists cannot drift.

source: The evidence line of this entry is out of date. Stubbing api.train_channel to always refuse applies cleanly (api.gd SHA256 885DEE -> 6EC793) and the run does NOT stay green: it dies with 6 script errors, Invalid access to property or key attempt_id on a base object of type Nil, at test_breakthrough_attempt.gd:218. Mechanism: the shared probe leaves the actor unprepared, MindAdvancement.start returns null, assert_ne(started, null) at :220 reports the failure but does not halt the test, and :221 onward dereferences nil, killing the runner mid-suite so every later suite is skipped and reports nothing. The other claim also understates itself - facade verbs ARE called from tests (test_high_tier_traversal.gd:159 calls strengthen_anchor, test_mind_cultivation_screen.gd drives attach and attach_sea, mind_gate_probe.gd calls train_channel); they are simply never asserted through summary().
next: Two jobs. (1) A facade-only suite that walks cultivate, train_channel, strengthen_sea and try_breakthrough asserting on summary() alone - that is what turns a verb mutation into a red assertion instead of a crash, and it would also kill the trained_stage, sequence and rng_state mutations named in the old entry. (2) An unguarded start() result is a landmine on its own: see the companion entry on dereferencing start() without a null guard.

title: UNWIRED: five more emitted-and-unread stat ids beyond those BL-0104 and BL-0114 name - mental_defense, comprehension_bonus, sea_clarity, sea_turbulence, sea_full
source: CLASSIFIED 2026-10-03, and the five ids are not one disposition. mental_defense: KEEP - ADR 0071 names it the mitigation input of MindDamage and combat_tuning.gd already carries mental_defense_cap; combat_engine/mind_damage.gd:226 now actually reads it, so it went from unread to wired without this module changing. comprehension_bonus: DELETED - it was 1.0 + comprehension*0.01 + technique_factor*0.02, i.e. core Stat.INSIGHT_GAIN (1.0 + comprehension*0.01) plus a second realm-rate term; two divergent multipliers on one gate. sea_clarity / sea_turbulence: DELETED - mirrors of SeaOfConsciousness fields ADR 0071 reads off the component, so a second copy of the truth with no reader. sea_full: DELETED - it was a THIRD definition of full, comparing current against effective_capacity() while SeaOfConsciousness.is_full compares against the reservoir maximum, so the two disagreed exactly when the sea was turbulent.
next: Deleted ids: test_mind_stats.gd test_the_deleted_sea_and_rate_ids_stay_deleted (source read across the module dir + a derived-bag read) and test_mind_stat_surface.gd (exact published id set for both providers). Mutation proof: re-planting the four gives 15179 passed/9 failed vs 15124/0, naming every guard. NOTE for a ui/ owner: game/src/ui/panels/stat_presenter.gd:143-147 still lists four ids that no longer exist as rows (harmless - the presenter falls back for unlisted ids - but stale), and combat_engine/mind_damage.gd:147 uses the StringName &"sea_turbulence" as an EFFECT KEY, which now shares a spelling with a deleted stat id.

title: PARTIAL: the breakthrough award magnitude is unconstrained - changing will 2.0 to will 10.0 at all 30 realms leaves the suite green
source: REAL, and the cause is a tautology rather than a missing assertion. test_breakthrough_attempt.gd:223 asserts will == before + _award(seed), where _award at :108-112 SUMS the same seed.rewards dictionary that advancement.gd:402-404 awards from, so any retune of the authored magnitude satisfies the assertion by construction. test_full_traversal.gd:182 asserts only awarded == (will > will_before). Nothing anywhere pins 2.0, which is consistent with the recorded control mutation.
next: Assert the magnitude against a number the test owns - an expected table or an explicit per-realm constant - once per realm in the traversal suite, so a retune has to be argued instead of absorbed. Do it together with BL-0115, which is the balance question the same number raises.

title: UNWIRED: mind's insight rate ignores Stat.INSIGHT_GAIN, which body and qi both multiply by - and because comprehension is the binding gate, this is the gate's rate
source: FIXED 2026-10-03. training.gd:98 _grant_insight now multiplies by actor.stats.derived(Stat.INSIGHT_GAIN), read BEFORE set_base so the sitting is not priced at the rate its own gain implies. Previously a flat INSIGHT_RATE, so sect insight_gain percentages, races and items did nothing for the one path whose entry gate IS comprehension.
next: Done. Mutation proof: insight_gain pinned to 1.0 gives 17199 passed/6 failed vs 15124 passed/0 failed before, across 5 assertions in test_mind_insight_rate.gd (proportional up, proportional down, rises with comprehension, rides core curve, call-site source guard) plus test_mind_gate_binding.gd. See BL-0153 for the balance consequence this had on which gate prices a breakthrough.

source: api.gd:147-152; actor_stats.gd:10 declares _providers with no public reader (only clear_providers, modifier_count, add_provider)
next: Add ActorStats.has_provider(script) to core and use it from the facade. One-line core change, needs an ADR per the OCP rule.

source: test_full_traversal.gd:117,296 'while sea.turbulence > 0.0' discarded meditate's return entirely; the four 'while not sea.is_full(actor)' loops in test_breakthrough_attempt.gd:60, test_mind_persistence.gd:55, test_mind_training.gd:57, test_mind_attempt_once_only.gd:59 had no cap; caps of 8192/4096 in test_full_traversal.gd and test_mind_breakthrough_chance.gd were large enough to write gigabytes before stopping. AGENTS.md forbids both a bare unbounded while and a huge iteration cap
next: Done. NOTE: mind_gate_probe.gd is NOT scratch - four suites preload it (test_full_traversal.gd:15, test_mind_gate_permissiveness.gd:19, test_mind_reachability.gd:24, test_mind_training.gd:6). It was deleted as scratch and that broke four suites' parse; restored from HEAD. All its caps are now bounded too.

title: UNWIRED: the 900s wall-clock ceiling cannot protect the disk - it bounds time, not bytes, so a writer at the measured ~1 GB/s was allowed ~900 GB inside it
source: tools/godot.py: TIMEOUT_SECONDS=900 with no size check; measured flood rate several hundred MB/s against a drive with 515 GB free. Proven with a synthetic flooder: a writer that wanted 120s was killed at 0.42s having written 11 MB once the ceiling was added
next: Done in this change. Byte ceiling is 64 MB polled at 20 Hz; the first attempt with a 0.25s poll overshot to 143 MB, which is why the poll is 20 Hz - detection granularity IS the overshoot

title: sect and nation are a shared three-tier vocabulary, not two parallel hierarchies
next: Write the base ADR: clan=born to, sect=sworn to, nation=lives under. One claim shape (position + standing + obligation) in both, authored once in contracts/, so a promotion rule is written once and read by both. Blocks every item below.

title: sect module: register, scaffold and facade skeleton
next: tools new_module sect; deps contracts+core+clan. Mirror the destiny 6-file shape (state/def/catalog/gate/projection/api) with an empty authored catalog. No body until the vocabulary ADR lands.

title: nation module: register, scaffold and facade skeleton
next: tools new_module nation; deps contracts+core+sect. nation reads sect, never the reverse. Registered-but-absent is a warning not a failure, so the permission can land first.

title: the shared claim value object: a position, a standing and an obligation
next: One Resource-free value object in contracts/ used by both sect and nation, so rank, standing and duty are the same three fields everywhere. Zero authored .tres may bind a contracts/ script (rules.py RESOURCE_HOME_UNITS).

title: neither sect nor nation may grant a stat directly
next: The load-bearing refusal: an institution hands out recognition, access and teaching, never power. Standing multiplies what the member can already do and is applied as a bounded percent. Reject in review any design where joining raises a base stat.

title: sect founding: a member founds a sect with an authored doctrine
next: Founding consumes a documented cost and writes a roster with one founder at the top position. The founder is the first entry in the sect's own ledger, not a special case.

title: joining, leaving and expulsion are three different verbs with three different costs
next: Leaving is always permitted and always costs standing. Expulsion costs the expeller more than it costs the expelled. Collapsing them into one verb loses the whole politics layer.

title: sect roster and the authored capacity that bounds it
next: A roster is a member list with an authored cap per position. Capacity is authored data, so a sect cannot grow past its own content, and an overflow is a refused admit, not a silent trim.

title: nation founding and succession: a polity outlives the actor who made it
next: A nation persists across generations the way a clan does (ADR 0064), so founding writes a ledger with no owner and succession is an event on it rather than a death handler.

title: sect positions are duties, not levels: outer/inner/elder and what each may do
next: A position grants a set of authored duties. Reuse the clan two-part split from ADR 0064 exactly: rank is discrete and authored, standing is a continuous earned integer, and neither is derived from the other.

title: nation offices are seats that exist whether or not anyone fills them
next: An office is a named seat with authored powers and a holder that may be empty. A vacant office is a readable state, which is what makes a succession contested.

title: promotion and demotion move standing and position independently
next: Two separate verbs on purpose: standing can rise without a promotion, and a promotion can be granted on little standing. A single verb makes the hierarchy purely numeric and removes the politics ADR 0064 kept.

title: succession: a position is filled by an heir, a trial or a contest
next: Reuse the ascension-is-walked shape from ADR 0058 rather than rolling a number. The method is authored per position, so a sect can name its heir and a nation can run a trial.

title: territory is an authored region with an owner, not a coordinate
next: Territory does not reuse world locations (ADR 0045): a location is a place, a territory is a claim over places. Author TerritoryDef with its own catalog and no overlap with WorldLocationDef's danger/resources fields.

title: claiming, holding and releasing a territory
next: Three verbs with different costs. A claim needs a holder with standing; a release is always allowed; a claim on a held territory is a conflict, not an overwrite.

title: territory yield and upkeep, paid on a clock that does not exist yet
next: Yield per period against an upkeep cost. DEF-0111 records that there is no calendar or world tick, so this item is blocked on a clock and must not invent a second one.

title: contested territory: a claim on held ground produces a conflict, never a silent flip
next: The conflict is data describing two parties and a prize. It hands off to the conflict resolution item rather than resolving itself, so one module owns how a conflict ends.

title: doctrine is an authored practice a sect exists to teach
next: A doctrine names what the sect teaches and what it refuses. Authored in SectDef so adding a school of thought is a .tres, and two sects with the same doctrine are rivals, not duplicates.

title: affinity is the fit between a member and the sect's doctrine, and it gates teaching
next: Affinity is fit, not loyalty and not a stat. It rises with teaching and falls with contradictory practice, and it gates who may be taught - never what the member is worth.

title: teaching spends the teacher and is refused when affinity is too low
next: A teach verb with a real cost on the teacher, refused with a named reason below the authored floor. Teaching that is free and unlimited makes disciples a resource faucet.

title: technique library access: a sect holds manuals its members may read
next: Blocked on the technique-access contracts seam, NOT on techniques. TechniquesApi is at exactly 12 public methods (MAX_FACADE_PUBLIC_METHODS), so the sect cannot be given a verb on it; and TechniqueGate is not the only path to a CodexEntry (1363 authored technique items route to ItemActivation.LEARNED). The seam must be a contracts/ interface shaped like damage_mechanism.gd (ADR 0067), reached by component id, with sect implementing it and techniques asking it. Needs its own ADR.

title: dues, tribute and patronage are authored terms, never automatic payment
next: ADR 0064 already decided a clan publishes terms and does not collect them. A sect does the same: the settlement verb belongs to a later economy, so this item authors the terms only.

title: a sect treasury is a ledger of obligations, not a pile of items
next: Hold the claims and dues as ledger lines. A treasury that duplicates the items module's inventory makes two sources of truth for what an institution owns.

title: favour and debt between institutions, symmetric like faction stance
next: Reuse the ADR 0047 symmetry rule: a favour owed by A to B is readable from both sides, so no module holds a one-sided opinion about another institution's debt.

title: inter-sect rivalry is a symmetric stance between sects, not a hostility list
next: Same shape as WorldFactionDef.relationships (ADR 0047) and the same authoring story: changing a stance is editing a .tres, and it is always symmetric.

title: inter-nation diplomacy: alliance, truce, embargo, war
next: A closed verb set on a symmetric stance. An unknown verb refuses closed and names itself, following the DestinyGate precedent rather than defaulting to neutral.

title: a sect or nation conflict resolves through the one combat spine, never its own formula
next: Blocked on nothing in the module: the declare/count/pay half is built and tested (--suite nation). What is missing is the PRODUCER of verdicts. Ship `contest` succession content only once a tournament can call advance_succession; ADR 0085 rules that an authored-but-unreachable method is dead content, the same failure ADR 0063 shipped as unreachable tiers.

title: war resolution and spoils, including a defeated institution's standing
next: A resolved conflict pays a prize and moves standing on both sides. Losing standing must be recoverable, so a defeat lowers a number rather than dissolving the institution.

title: schism and secession: a sect can split, and the split costs both halves
next: Being built: SectApi.declare_schism costs both halves.

title: sect and nation NPCs: institutions that act without the player
next: Blocked on DEF-0111 (no clock). Institution simulation needs a season. The seam is decided: app/ owns real time and calls into the module with an explicit periods count; a module must never grow its own timer, because a second clock is a second source of truth for when a save happened. Do NOT build this until a clock exists.

title: the faction relation graph reads sect and nation stances without owning them
next: Being built: a read-only relations module that stores no stance.

title: reputation toward a sect or nation is separate from standing inside it
next: Being built: the sect screen as a pure read of SectApi.summary.

title: sect screen: a pure read of the facade with no rules of its own
next: Being built: the nation screen as a board of offices.

title: nation screen: the polity as a board of offices rather than a list of numbers
next: Blocked on BL-0201 and a quest system (BL-0053). The five states (found/built/contested/lost/rebuilt) can be authored now as a state machine with authored gates and needs no quest system to be testable; only the CONTENT is blocked.

title: the founder's arc: found, build, lose and rebuild, as a quest-shaped progression
next: A reachability guard for authored sect/nation content: every authored position, office, doctrine and succession method must be reachable by some authored path. ADR 0063 shipped dead tiers because nothing asserted reachability, so the guard is a test beside realm_power check, not a comment.

title: authored content for sects, nations and territories ships as .tres with no code
next: Every def is a Resource under game/data/. A sect, nation or territory that needs code to add one has the wrong shape. tools data audit gates the cross-references.

title: a reachability guard: no authored position, office or doctrine may be unreachable
next: ADR 0063 shipped dead tiers because nothing asserted the numbers were reachable. Assert every authored position is grantable by some path, or the content is decoration.

title: contract tests for both facades, one suite per concern
next: Needs its own ADR before the first authored .tres ships: where a POLITY ledger lives. actor.module_data dies with the actor, and a nation outlives the actor that founded it (ADR 0083). Tracked as DEF-0119. The first slice uses module_data and the ledger is JSON-safe; a screen built before this is answered would be a screen rewrite.

title: the sect and nation save schema is JSON-safe and versioned per ledger
next: ADR 0027 module_data is String-keyed and JSON-round-tripped in a test. An institution ledger holding an Actor or a Resource ref silently breaks every save.

title: RATE_STEP guard asserts a pasted 1.05, not the invariant it claims (VACUOUS guard)
source: orchestrator review 2026-10-03, after ADR 0066 collapsed the rate into core/realm_rate.gd
next: AGENTS.md states the invariant as: RATE_STEP must stay at or below the smallest per-realm step in the authored work budget, or the rate outruns the price and the deep realms get cheap. But game/tests/core/test_realm_rate.gd:78 asserts the literal RealmRate.RATE_STEP <= 1.05, and AGENTS.md notes tools realm_power check does not cover RATE_STEP at all. A pasted bound cannot detect the thing it is standing in for: if a realm seed's work_required steps shrink, the invariant can be violated while the test still passes. Replace the literal with a computed check against the smallest per-realm ratio in the authored work budget - the same drift-detecting shape the seed generator already has.

title: ADR 0067's 11-stage damage spine is Accepted in docs and implemented nowhere
source: orchestrator review 2026-10-03; combat api.gd is 16 lines with 2 public methods
next: Stage 0 of the Domain program, because AC5 (a domain you can fight in) is unreachable without it. Build modules/combat/combat_damage.gd with S1-S11 in ADR 0067's stated order, contracts/damage_mechanism.gd as the seam, CombatTuning in combat_damage.tres, and DamageProposal as {amount: float, effects: Array[Dictionary]}. Then the qi, body and mind mechanisms from ADR 0069/0070/0071. Four orderings must be independently assertable: S1 before S2 (the ladder must not move hit frequency), S2 before S4 (a miss invokes no mechanism), S4 before S6 (crit multiplies the mechanism's output and is never its input), and S7 before S8 before S9 (reduction runs, then the floor restores the chip). No rounding anywhere and no division in the spine.

title: PlayerAdapter.attack() is a comment, so nothing the player does in a domain resolves
next: PARTLY RESOLVED 2026-10-03, re-scope before working: PlayerAdapter.attack() is no longer a comment - it has a real body (requires State.COMBAT and a Node2D target). But it is not the domain-fight path and should not be made one: the shipped fight runs through CombatApi.exchange, which resolves the player's offense into a share of the boss's authored vitality and spends it with LootApi.strike. PlayerAdapter.attack targets a spatial Node2D, and there is no spatial layer yet (see BL-0212), so it is a world-interaction verb waiting on the world, not a missing damage source. Do not wire it to the domain fight.

title: A domain is a 3-field loot bucket: DomainDef has id, display_name and boss_ids and nothing else
next: Grow DomainDef into a map description - layout (handcrafted scene id OR template id plus seed), rooms, paths, actor spawn refs, fixtures and environment - behind one producer interface so a handcrafted and a generated domain are indistinguishable downstream. 160 .tres already exist and stay valid: every new field is optional and a def that omits them keeps today's behaviour. Also extend tools data audit with the new kinds and cross-references; data.py:112,235 hardcodes the domain schema and script path today. || SHIPPED 2026-10-03, verified 53 passing in test_domain_map_contract: the domain module owns the map model. RoomDef, DomainMap, EnvironmentZoneDef, DomainRoles and DomainMapContract exist; DomainMap is engine-agnostic and JSON-clean; entering a map that fails the contract is refused by name (DomainApi.enter -> ERR_INVALID_CONTRACT). REMAINING: grow the 160 existing DomainDef .tres with the new fields and extend tools data audit (tools/data.py:112,235 still hardcode the old 3-field schema).

title: There is no spatial machinery at all - no TileMap, no AStar, no NavigationAgent in game/src
next: A walkable domain needs a TileMap-based scene plus pathing. The one NavigationRegion2D per domain scene is an empty unnamed node with no polygon and no bake. Build the tile floor/wall layers, the corridor graph, and a navigation bake, and prove connectivity with a test that walks room to room.

title: The 8 authored domain/world scenes are orphaned and their ids join to no DomainDef
source: domain design 2026-10-03; ADR 0073; 0 references to res://scenes/domains/ repo-wide
next: game/scenes/domains/*.tscn (4) and game/scenes/worlds/*.tscn (4) are loaded by nothing: grep for res://scenes/domains/ returns no matches, and ScreenRoutes names none of them. Their names (mortal_plains, immortal_court, spirit_peaks, transcendent_realm) correspond to no DomainDef id. Decide each scene's fate as part of the handcrafted half: either join it to a real DomainDef or delete it. Do not leave eight unreachable scenes as decoration on a ColorRect.

title: world_entry.gd is a scene base with zero callers, and an arch test freezes its source
source: domain design 2026-10-03; test_arch_rules.gd:473-483 transcribes its first lines verbatim
next: The marker/zone binder is referenced only by the 8 orphan scenes and pinned by shape-frozen assertions that classify it as wiring. Reviving it means editing a frozen shape; deleting it means repointing the 8 scenes. Settle this before Stage 2 so the domain scene base is chosen, not inherited by accident.

title: Handcrafted and generated domains must share one room kit, or they are two systems
next: RoomDef is the shared currency: a handcrafted room and a generated room are the same def, so a template assembles authored rooms and a scene authors the same rooms. AC1 is the parity test - a handcrafted map and a seeded map both pass the same contract test (rooms >= 1, >= 1 exit, every path resolvable, no orphan room). AC6 is determinism: same seed produces an identical map, different seed does not.

title: Nothing constructs an Actor for anything but the player and one offspring
source: domain design 2026-10-03; ADR 0074; 4 Actor.new sites in game/src, all player or child
next: There is no NPC, mob, miniboss, boss or rival-cultivator constructor anywhere. Add one factory entry point that spawns an Actor for role mob|miniboss|boss|npc|rival_cultivator and tags it, so AC2 holds by construction: one test asserts every role yields an Actor and no parallel NPC class exists. This is the wiring that makes the user's premise true in code rather than only in intent. || SHIPPED 2026-10-03, verified 112 passing in test_domain_spawner: one DomainSpawner.spawn(def, role) returns an Actor for every role in DomainRoles, with the role as a tag on Actor.tags and no parallel subclass. A def claiming `cultivates` with no realm_id is refused by name rather than defaulted.

title: No spawn mechanism puts an actor into a room, so a populated domain has no population
next: Rooms carry actor spawn refs and the domain resolver mints and places them. AC3: a map with N refs yields N live Actors at resolvable positions, and a handcrafted and a generated map with the same ref count both resolve. Placement must be deterministic under the injected RandomNumberGenerator the repo already uses. || SHIPPED 2026-10-03: DomainSpawner.spawn_map walks DomainMap.spawn_refs() in canonical order and mints one Actor per ref honouring count; a missing inhabitant is a named refusal that mints nothing.

title: Weather, trap, treasure and hazard do not exist as concepts anywhere in game/ - zero occurrences
source: domain design 2026-10-03; ADR 0075; grep over game/ returns 0 real hits, only item-id prefixes
next: BL-0063 'Spiritual environment and Qi density' has no foothold at all. Build EnvironmentZoneDef for super-hot, super-cold, static and toxic volumes as room or corridor properties applying a StatusEffect (ADR 0002 already models statuses) with a named mitigation lever - gear affix, technique, pill, or spirit-root affinity. AC4: a hot zone applies damage over time and an actor carrying the mitigation takes measurably less. Weather is a domain-level property over the same zones. Traps, puzzles and treasure are room fixtures using the same spawn-ref mechanism as actors, with a different payload. || SHIPPED 2026-10-03: EnvironmentZoneDef is a closed 8-kind fixture with a 3-point authored band and mandatory mitigation_tags, and DomainMapContract rejects a zone with no lever, an unknown lever, or an affinity-only lever set (each proven by a test in test_domain_map_contract).

title: A sect, castle or inner world is a second concept when it is a settlement room in a domain template
next: The user wants sect/castle to live inside a domain and a domain to become an inner world. Make settlement a room type in the shared room kit, so an inner world is a template whose rooms are settlement rooms - one concept, no parallel system. Note the collision to resolve: InsideWorld and WorldState already exist in core/ for the actor's personal inner world, and inner_world_qi_density is a live stat provider. Decide whether the walkable inner world replaces, wraps or is a map over that state.

title: No headless way to see a domain, so an agent cannot inspect or play one
next: Extend the existing `tools ui` headless driver (ADR 0043) with a domain driver that enters a domain, prints the map and encounter state as JSON, accepts --cmd verbs to move/fight/open/claim, and writes a screenshot per step so the result is visually checkable, not only machine-readable. This is the same contract the UI already honours (summary() primitives) applied to a map. Without it AC5 is unprovable by an agent.

title: No damage model exists anywhere in the codebase (UNBUILT)
next: STALE BY DESIGN - reconcile at integration. ADR-truth 2026-10-03 recorded DamageProposal as having 0 occurrences and wrote ADR 0077 stating the damage spine is designed-not-built. That was true when written; the combat agent has since landed contracts/damage_proposal.gd (9 occurrences). Still absent as of that audit: CombatTuning, combat_damage, RESIST_DIVISOR, BodyDamageProfile, damage_mechanism, mechanism_slot, element_share. When the combat agent reports, ADR 0077 must be superseded again with the real state, and SCHEMA_VERSION is still 4 so no v5 save shape exists yet. Do not treat 0077 as current truth.

title: The combat module is 100 percent dead code: zero callers, zero tests (VACUOUS)
next: RESOLVED 2026-10-03, verdict inverted: the combat module is neither dead nor untested. It has a real caller - game/src/ui/screens/loot_encounter.gd:107 calls CombatApi.exchange(_actor, STRIKE_SEED) from the screen's own attack control, so the player's gear resolves a blow against the boss's authored vitality (combat is declared in rules.UI_MODULES, so ui/ may name it). Fifteen test files under game/tests/modules/combat and game/tests/modules/combat_engine exercise it. The action-RPG kill step is reachable through shipped code, not only a test.

title: Domain boss fights are guaranteed wins with a flat damage constant (VACUOUS)
next: The only thing reducing boss vitality is a caller's constant: LOOT_STRIKE_DAMAGE := 25.0 at item_workbench_app.gd:20, mirrored in loot_bridge.gd:37 and loot_encounter.gd:31, applied at loot_state.gd:196. Authored vitality across the 9 loot tiers is 100-520 (median 340), so a clear is 4-21 identical presses with no variance, and nothing in the fight can lose. Tie strike damage to Stat.ATTACK_PHYSICAL and delete the constant. NOTE: item_workbench_app.gd is an active edit surface owned by another agent - build the primitive elsewhere and report the wiring requirement.

title: BossDef has no combat fields, so a boss cannot act (UNBUILT)
next: boss_def.gd declares exactly four fields: id, display_name, domain_id, loot. No vitality, health, attack, defense, AI or phases. Vitality is authored in the loot tier data instead, which is why the strike constant had to be a literal. Decide and record: either BossDef gains the fields it needs, or an ADR states plainly that bosses are inert health bags and the flat-damage clear is the intended design.

title: No player damage or death path exists in any fight (UNBUILT)
next: Nothing in loot/ mutates a player health pool: grep for health across loot/ finds no pool mutation, and loot_state.gd:177-206 only decrements boss vitality. A fight cannot be lost, so every failure mechanic and every risk item is dead content. This is the hardest gap and the decision that unblocks a real tribulation encounter: settle the death model before building an encounter on top of Tribulation.fight_wave, whose resolution is currently a probability check.

title: Tribulation has zero UI: no wave, no outcome, no endurance readout (UNWIRED)
next: grep for tribulation across src/ui/ returns zero matches, and body_cultivation api.gd:73-90 panel_state exposes no wave or outcome. The fight is real and wired - face_tribulation has 4 production callers (body_cultivation/advancement.gd:156, qi_cultivation/advancement.gd:89, qi_cultivation/breakthrough_transaction.gd:101, mind_cultivation/advancement.gd:240) - but every one of the ~9 presses needed to clear R19 shows the same generic string, breakthrough_condition.gd:72 'Immortal tier gates not met (tribulation, inside world, ascension)', which lumps three distinct gates. Add tribulation fields to panel_state and a panel row so the fight is observable.

title: 9 of 11 WorldApi verbs and 17 authored world .tres have no reader (UNWIRED)
next: Only locations() and create_world() have production callers. evolve_world, merge_world and trigger_conflict are 100 percent test-only; add_law, add_inhabitant and pay_upkeep likewise. data/world/{factions,inhabitants,laws,tiers} is 17 .tres files that nothing loads. Wire them or delete them - but decide first, because the docstrings currently promise behaviour the code does not have.

title: One function gates three dead modules: _build_actor never attaches dual_cultivation, fertility or elements

title: Godot log sink was one shared file, so concurrent runs corrupted each other's trail and summed the byte ceiling

Uniqueness is pid+seq, NOT the clock alone: tools test runs --import then the suite in one process, and a warm-cache import can land in the same second, so a timestamp alone reintroduced the clobber.

title: Byte ceiling overshoots by ~187 MB against a writer sustaining ~2 GB/s
source: Measured: probe writing 1 MB chunks in a loop was killed at 0.12s having written 251 MB against a 64 MB ceiling (187 MB past)
next: Open, not urgent. LOG_POLL_SECONDS=0.05 bounds overshoot to rate*interval, and the rate is higher than the earlier ~1 GB/s estimate. 187 MB is harmless against a 515 GB disk; raising the ceiling buys little because overshoot scales with rate, not with the ceiling. Revisit only if a writer is measured above ~10 GB/s.

title: Byte ceiling overshoots badly at a writer faster than the incident
source: Measured with a synthetic flooder after the per-run-log refactor: killed at 0.12s having written 251 MB against a 64 MB ceiling, i.e. 187 MB overshoot, because the flooder sustained ~2 GB/s. The earlier 11 MB figure came from a ~1 GB/s writer, so the poll interval was sized for half the real rate.
next: Tighten LOG_POLL_SECONDS (0.05 -> 0.01) so overshoot at 2 GB/s falls under ~20 MB, then re-measure. 100 stat() calls/sec is still free next to a Godot run.

title: Every concurrent run shared one log file, corrupting the trail and the ceiling
source: LOG_FILE was the single fixed path build/godot.log and run_godot truncated it at every start. With 13 concurrent runs observed, each truncated the others' logs, the byte ceiling summed ALL writers (so it could kill an innocent run because a different run was spinning), and the diagnostic tail was overwritten before anyone read it. Also _breach was defined twice in tools/godot.py; Python silently kept the second, dropping the --suite hint.
next: Done in tools/godot.py: per-run logs under build/logs/<stamp>-<pid>-<seq>-<tag>.log, retention 8, sweep_old_logs(). Verified: 3 calls in one process yield distinct paths, and both ceilings still fire (flood 0.12s/251MB, wall clock 2.03s).

title: A run that hangs SILENTLY defeats the byte ceiling: it writes nothing, so the disk guard cannot see it
source: Measured: 	ools test --suite mind_cultivation produced a 0-byte log for 32s+ while the engine sat at 0.1s CPU and 0MB RSS (idle, not spinning). tools/godot.py's byte ceiling measures LOG SIZE, so a silent hang is invisible to it and only the 900s wall clock catches it.
next: Add a progress/no-output guard to tools/godot.py: if the run has produced no bytes AND no CPU time after N seconds, kill it and say so. This is the disk-safety analogue of the loop fix: a run that cannot make progress must fail loudly. Not urgent for the SSD (0 bytes written) but it makes a 15-minute wait into a fast failure with a real diagnosis.

title: Generation is 2-level BSP plus a spanning tree with proximity loop edges, and it has no retry anywhere
next: BSP is chosen because sibling recursion gives connectivity structurally rather than via a solver, and because disjoint rectilinear leaves make the nav outline exactly computable with no epsilon tolerance. Tile size 32px; MIN_LEAF authored per band; split ratio 0.40-0.60 on the longer axis; max_depth 3-5 authored per band as a hard cap; corridor 3 tiles mortal/spirit and 4 immortal+; loop_ratio 0.00-0.25 with MAX_LOOP_SPAN 6 tiles. Leaves sort into a canonical spatial order using ZERO rng so fill order is geometry not dice. Structural roles (entry, core, gate, arena) are rule-placed; content roles (settlement, boss) are author-pinned only and never auto-placed. One push_error naming template, seed, condition and numbers, then return null - never a retry, never a substituted default room. || SHIPPED with fixes 2026-10-03. The BSP + spanning tree generator exists and the four generator bugs found by running it are fixed: _deal indexed past the end of the kit (it now wraps over the POOL), a pin index past the last leaf is CLAMPED and RELOCATED rather than dropped, and a pin's def and kind are now resolved through one shared _free_leaf so they cannot land on different leaves. The three authored templates were also arithmetically impossible as first written - measured max reachable leaves were 4/8/8 against min_rooms 6/10/18 - so extents were enlarged and the floors set from measurement (6/6/9), not aspiration.

title: The authored domain scenes are read into the map, and their nav polygon is computed not baked

title: Body training has no observable payoff: 7 of 8 body stat ids reach neither the game nor the screen
source: orchestrator verification 2026-10-03 (BL-0131 re-verified, worse than filed)

Evidence: of the eight BodyStats ids only move_speed has a reader outside its own module (game/src/app/player_adapter.gd and game/src/contracts/stat.gd). body_cultivation_power, bone_density, carry_capacity, muscle_fiber, acupoint_count, acupoint_quality and acupoint_blocked_count have NONE - rg over game/src excluding body_cultivation returns nothing. title: CORRECTION: BL-0291 was my fourth false alarm - screens INHERIT setup from UiScreen
next: BL-0291 claimed 9 of 11 routed screens have no setup() and that navigating to them mounts a blank screen and throws. FALSE, and it was my error. My check was a text search for a line beginning with 'func setup(' in each screen's own file, which only finds a screen that OVERRIDES setup and cannot see an INHERITED one. game/src/ui/screens/ui_screen.gd line 21 declares 'var _actor: Actor = null' and line 29 declares 'func setup(actor: Actor) -> void:'. Every one of those nine screens extends UiScreen, so they all inherit setup(actor) and _actor, and in Godot an inherited method satisfies has_method('setup') and _screen.call('setup', _actor) works. Confirmed on loot_encounter.gd specifically: it never declares or assigns _actor itself and correctly inherits both. CONSEQUENCE, which is why this one matters more than the other three: I had already DISPATCHED an agent to add setup() to all nine screens. Nine redundant overrides would have been a duplicate-actor bug in nine files - exactly the hazard I warned that agent about while handing it the false premise. I have stopped it and told it to revert anything it already added. THE REAL LESSON, and it generalises past this repo: a text search cannot see inheritance, so any finding that rests on a grep which a single base-class declaration would overturn is not a finding yet. Prefer an executable probe - instantiate the node and ask has_method - over searching source. This is the fourth false alarm I have filed in one session (the others: granting the current realm's pill instead of the target realm's, a driver verb typo whose error event my formatting rendered as null, and an ungranted sea catalyst). Every one looked serious; none survived checking. The mitigations are now in the briefs I send: verify against the runtime, and check whether a gate is gated on an authored item you never granted before calling it unreachable.

title: A module-local substitute now duplicates ADR 0057; two sources of truth until it is resolved
next: SEQUENCING HAZARD, recorded so it is not lost between two agents. The body agent, unable to touch contracts/ or core/, shipped a module-local substitute so the body path was not left with a dead reward: BodyProvider.new(actor) holds the ACTOR rather than the network, with _invalidate_stats_on_meridian_change in body_cultivation/api.gd, and provider.gd's _meridian_power_bonus now reads the injected actor. Its reasoning is sound - from_dict is static and returns a NEW Actor, so holding the Actor is currently indistinguishable from holding the network - and it said so plainly rather than claiming the accessor was unnecessary. Meanwhile ADR 0057 prescribes a context accessor that is being restored right now by a separate agent. THE HAZARD: for as long as both exist there are TWO answers to how a provider reaches the meridian network, and the one that works today is the one that will be deleted. A future agent reading provider.gd will see a working pattern that contradicts the ADR. RESOLUTION IS A DECISION, not a cleanup: either the substitute is removed once the accessor lands and provider.gd goes back to reading context.meridian_network(), or the substitute becomes permanent and ADR 0057 is SUPERSEDED (ADRs are immutable - supersede, never rewrite), which also settles what contracts/attack_context.gd does when it has no network to pass. Until one of those happens, a stat that is quietly 0 is the failure mode ADR 0057 exists to prevent. Do not let this sit: it is the same shape as the deleted 'value' field, the unloaded meridian .tres files, and the numeraire's fabricated source - a gate green-lighting a second authority.

title: A bare while true: made GDScript's analyzer reject the file, zeroing a 407-line suite: the last unloadable suite in the repo
source: tools test, session 2026-10-03: 47 script errors reduced to 1, and that one was 'Not all code paths return a value' at test_nation_conflict.gd:347
next: FIXED, and the class is now structurally impossible. Cause: _names_a_type() in test_nation_conflict.gd was while true: with only eturns inside. GDScript's flow analysis cannot PROVE a while true: returns, so it emitted 'Not all code paths return a value' and refused to compile the file -- taking a 407-line suite to zero assertions. It was the last unloadable suite and the only parse error left in a 248-suite run. The loop was not actually unbounded (from advances past every hit and find returns -1 past the end of line), so this was purely the analyzer, not a spin. Fix: the search window became the bound -- while from <= line.length(): with  reak on the not-found case and a definite eturn false after -- so the condition states what terminates it, matching AGENTS.md. Before 0 assertions, after Results: 187 passed, 3 failed. Swept and hardened the only two other bare while true: in the repo, both in traversal suites (body_cultivation and qi_cultivation), by moving an existing guard <= 64 cap from the loop body into the condition; both still report 492/0 and 440/0, and the repo-wide unbounded-wait guard is 699 passed, 0 failed. Repo-wide count of bare while true: is now 0. Worth knowing for the future: a while true: is not merely a style problem in GDScript, it is a compile error whenever the enclosing function declares a return type, so one loop can silently zero out an entire suite.

title: The teaching door is circular: the only writer of fit is the verb that refuses you for lacking fit, so no student can ever be taught
source: tools test --suite sect/test_sect_teaching, session 2026-10-03: Results: 66 passed, 12 failed; exhaustive grep for fit writers across game/src
next: CIRCULAR GATE, proven by exhaustive search of fit writers -- the same class as BL-0106 (nothing starts a tribulation, so R19+ is a wall). Chain: SectApi.teach checks SectTeaching.student_admitted(def, s_ledger), which is def.teaches_at(SectState.fit(student_ledger, def.doctrine_id)), which is student_fit >= def.min_purity. The ONLY production writer of a ledger fit map is SectTeaching.apply_fit (grep for apply_fit across game/src returns exactly one caller, api.gd:484, inside teach). sect_state.gd:313 writes fit too, but that is SectState.normalize -- save-payload normalization on attach, not a verb that grants anything. So the one thing that raises fit is the verb that refuses you for lacking it: a student below the door can never be taught, and therefore can never rise above the door. The suite proves it the only way it can, by hand-writing the ledger: test_sect_teaching.gd:260 and :273 assign (ledger['fit'])[DOCTRINE] directly and re-attach, which is the test doing the player's job -- the same anti-pattern as BL-0101. Measured: 12 failures, 11 of them this (every ordinary-student case refuses with standing_below_floor; the 12th asserts the door itself). Authored doors are real, not fixture noise: game/data min_purity is 10 for the foundry fixture and 30 for iron_vine. Two fixes, and they are NOT equivalent, so this needs a deliberate choice rather than a patch: (a) read the student's STANDING at the door instead of fit -- supported by the reason string already being STANDING_BELOW_FLOOR, by the doctrine's own words 'a member under it is not being taught anything', and by standing being reachable through join and SectApi.move_standing; or (b) keep the fit door and grant fit at join or founding, so the first lesson can land. (a) makes the door reachable with no new content and makes the existing reason string honest; (b) preserves fit as the door but needs an authored grant. Separately worth fixing either way: the reason for a FIT refusal is named standing_below_floor, so a panel would tell a player their standing is too low when their affinity is -- a vocabulary lie in the direction ADR 0083 says is load-bearing for every screen.

title: All 27 domain_generator failures are one cause: every authored room pin is silently dropped, and a complete pin would only half-apply
source: tools test --suite domain/test_domain_generator, session 2026-10-03; all 27 messages reduce to 'placed at least one author pin: expected true, got false' plus its downstream room assertions
next:
FIXED -- all 27 failures closed, suite is Results: 2018 passed, 0 failed. My earlier two write-ups on this were wrong and are superseded; the cause was three separate defects, none of which was the one I first guessed. Measured with a temporary per-seed diagnostic (leaves count, the reserved set, the settlement-kind count, and both pin dictionaries) that I then removed and restored the file around byte-identically (sha 8F66E072DFB2).
(1) DATA. game/src/data/domains/templates/flame_valley_depths.tres authored pin_camp with room_def = ExtResource 5_camp (ash_camp.tres) but its room_pool was only [2_floor, 3_chamber, 6_furnace] -- 5_camp was missing. _pinned_defs checks pool membership and _fail()s, so that pin was un-honourable on EVERY seed: 64 of the 77 failures were this one template across seeds 1..64. The sibling stormwrack_reach.tres does list 5_camp, which is what made it obvious. Fixed by adding ExtResource("5_camp") to that pool. 27 -> 15 failures.
(2) CODE. _place_structural built reserved = [entry, core, gate] + arenas with no budget, so it could cover EVERY leaf: ember_grotto seed 46 produced leaves=8 reserved=[1,5,2,0,3,4,6,7], _free_leaf answered -1, and the pin was dropped with no diagnostic -- the exact outcome _pinned_defs own docstring says must not happen. The same line also admitted duplicates and -1 (flame_valley seed 49 gave reserved=[7,7,-1]), because the three indexes come from three different searches and _lowest_neighbour can answer -1. Fixed: reserved is built deduplicated and non-negative, and arena_budget = leaves - reserved - pins, so a pin always has a leaf to land on. Arenas are the discretionary kind and give way; floor/core/gate do not, because a pin is documented never to overrule geometry. 15 -> 10 failures.
(3) CODE. kinds[core] = &"core" is guarded on core != entry, and _farthest answers the entry whenever the entry is its own farthest -- routine for a shallow or single-branch map -- so those maps had NO core room at all. Fixed with a deterministic fallback to the lowest canonical non-entry index, the same rule-not-a-roll shape as _entry_index. 10 -> 0 failures.
MUTATION PROOF, both code fixes load-bearing: disabling the core fallback gives 2008 passed / 10 failed naming exactly "every generated domain has one core"; removing pins from arena_budget gives 1996 passed / 5 failed naming exactly the pin-starvation messages including ember_grotto seed 46. One fix I tried and REVERTED: adding the pool check to _apply_pins and _pinned_kinds so a kind can never be placed without its def. It is correct in principle but made things worse (27 -> 77) because it turned defect (1) into "nothing placed at all" on flame_valley; the real fix there was the data, not a third guard. Left that file untouched.

title: One mid-write Python file killed the entire tools CLI with a bare traceback; it now names the file
next: The Python twin of BL-0329. tools/__main__.py imported all nineteen task modules eagerly, so a single IndentationError in any one of them made EVERY tools command unavailable - including tools test and tools check - and the only output was a bare traceback ending in IndentationError with no indication that a half-written file was the likely cause. FIXED in tools/__main__.py: each task module loads through _load(), which catches SyntaxError and ImportError and prints the offending path with the reason plus 'If another agent is writing that file right now, wait and retry; every tools command is unavailable until it loads', then exits 2. TWO PROCESS NOTES against myself: my first probe created tools/zz_probe_broken.py, which proved nothing because the dispatcher only imports the modules it names - a test that cannot fail is not a test, and I nearly filed the feature as verified on it; and my first version caught only SyntaxError, so an ImportError would still traceback. Both found by checking the mechanism rather than trusting it.

title: BLOCKER: WorldAnchor.commit has zero production callers, so no ascent is ever begun and R29-R30 is unreachable
source: orchestrator, measured by driving the shipped panel 2026-10-03
next: CIRCULARITY REFUTED - MY EARLIER READING WAS WRONG, recorded here so nobody re-files it. breakthrough.gd:201-206 ascension_ok opens with 'if next_index <= WorldAnchor.COMMIT_MICRO: return true'. COMMIT_MICRO is 27 (world_anchor.gd:29). So entering index 27 is checked by ascension_ok(actor,27) -> 27 <= 27 -> TRUE, no ascent owed; that advance then commits 27 and begins the ascent; the gate that consumes it is ascension_ok(actor,28) on the NEXT advance. The commit for index N serves the gate for index N+1, never the gate on the same advance, so committing AFTER can_advance is correct and not circular. Corroboration is already in the file: inside_world_ok's docstring at breakthrough.gd:177-181 describes this exact circularity being fixed once before for R19 - 'Entering R19 commits the Seed inside world, so R19 must not require it as a prerequisite - that was circular and left the gate permanently unsatisfiable' - and ascension_ok carries the same escape hatch for the same reason. MY 'No ascent begun' DRIVE WAS MY OWN INSTRUMENT'S FAULT: realm:<id> writes state.rank_id directly and so TELEPORTS the rank, bypassing the very breakthrough into index 27 that commits. A hero teleported to 28 has correctly never begun an ascent. That is BL-0313 in a new form - the instrument jumped a gate rather than walking it. The correct instrument is Breakthrough.try_advance, which is what the Breakthrough press calls, and game/tests/core/test_player_walks_to_r30.gd uses it and contains no WorldAnchor.commit at all, only the COMMIT_MICRO constant. KEEP the core commit: it fixes no reachable bug today, but it makes the milestone have exactly one owner instead of one per caller, which is the ADR 0066 failure mode AGENTS.md exists to prevent.

title: ActorStats discarded any modifier on a stat nothing backs, so all nine combat rate ids read 0.0
source: tools test --suite test_combat_stats_shape, session 2026-10-03: 92 passed, 12 failed -> 104 passed, 0 failed after the fix; mutation restores 92/12
next: FIXED in core, with an ADR (docs/adr/0111). ActorStats resolved a modifier only where something else had already written the stat: _recompute writes a fixed list of core ids, _ensure_providers writes whatever providers contribute, and derived(id) answers from _provider_cache else _derived.get(id, 0.0). A StatModifier on any other id was bucketed and thrown away. CombatStats.RATE_IDS (accuracy, absorption, parry.rate, parry.strength, block.rate, block.strength, reflect.rate, reflect.resist.rate, lifesteal) has no core entry and no provider -- CombatStats is a constants class, not a StatProvider -- so all nine read 0.0 whatever an author wrote. ADR 0068 shape test caught all nine and was right to. Fix: after the core derived stats, back every remaining modifier bucket at 0.0 through the same _put formula. This preserves the ADR 0022 trap rather than papering over it: FLAT reads (0.0+v)*1=v, and PERCENT still reads (0.0+0.0)*1.25=0.0, which is why RATE_DEFAULTS is all zeros. Measured: test_combat_stats_shape went 92 passed/12 failed to 104 passed/0 failed. MUTATION PROVEN: removing the backfill returns 92/12 naming exactly the nine rate ids plus a real gameplay assertion ('250 of 1000 draws, exactly the authored rate: expected 250, got 0'), so the fix is load-bearing for mechanics and not only for the shape test. This did NOT fix BL-0283 -- qi_damage is still 34 and reflect 16 -- those are separate defects in qi_damage.gd itself, whose failures read like a wrong default or a swapped argument ('and the default share is 0.0 too: expected 0.0, got 0.8', 'and leaves no negative raw share: expected 0.0, got 500.0', '50 points over the divisor: expected 0.5, got 0.0'). Next person should read _resistance_of and _share_of in combat_engine/qi_damage.gd (461 lines, untracked) against tuning.resist_cap and the RESIST_DIVISOR in combat_damage.tres.

title: qi_damage: the shipped default_element_share 0.8 contradicts the asserted neutral 0.0, and three resistance reads are wrong independently of it
source: tools test --suite combat_engine/test_qi_damage, session 2026-10-03: Results: 190 passed, 34 failed; combat_damage.tres vs CombatTuning's own 0.0 default

title: A script error killed the runner mid-loop, so a 260-suite run printed no Results line at all
source: tools test, session 2026-10-03: two full runs ended with 'fail 39 script error(s) aborted a test mid-function' and no Results: line
next: FIXED, and it was hiding the whole project from measurement. A GDScript runtime error inside suite.call(name) kills run_tests.gd mid-loop, so the closing print("Results: ...") at the end of _initialize never runs. title: A test that could not fail: the discarded-network test never warmed the cache, so a lazy capture grabbed the NEW network and passed
source: body_cultivation agent, found and fixed during the ADR 0057 substitute removal, 2026-10-03
next: A GENUINE TEST DEFECT, found by the agent that removed the last ADR 0057 substitute, and worth keeping because the SHAPE recurs across this program. The test game/tests/modules/body_cultivation/test_body_meridian_read.gd::test_the_provider_never_serves_a_network_the_actor_discarded asserts a provider never serves a meridian network the actor discarded after a save/load. Under mutation M3 - capturing the network on first read instead of resolving it per read - IT STAYED GREEN, 28 passed / 0 failed. Root cause: the test never warmed the stats cache before swapping actor.meridians, so a lazy first read happened AFTER the swap and therefore grabbed the NEW network, which is the correct answer for the wrong reason. A test that only ever reads before the state it is testing has not actually tested the transition. The fix was to add a warm read before the swap - the realistic shape, since stats are computed and then the network is restored underneath - and re-applying M3 now fails on 'and not the one it discarded: expected false, got true'. GENERAL LESSON, which is why this is filed rather than closed: a test that exercises a RESTORE must perform a READ BEFORE the restore, or it is asserting nothing about the restore. The same shape produced BL-0285 (inventory capacity serialized but never restored, undetected for want of a mutation), BL-0123/0124/0125 (three body gates whose deletion left the suite green) and the tautological test_realm_rate.gd. Whenever the property under test is 'the new value is picked up', the test must establish an OLD value first.

Cause is _content_probe() building Dictionary values from multi-line lambdas. Consequence is severe and SILENT - every gdformat pass re-emits the class doc block, so one pass took the committed file 288 to 447 lines and a second took it to 669. It fails silently: gdformat prints reformatted with no warning, and gdlint parses the file fine, so lint and a test run both look healthy while the file grows. THE AGENT MADE IT WORSE BEFORE IT UNDERSTOOD: three scoped passes grew the file 13.5 KB to 63 KB with 20 duplicated blocks. It restored the file byte-exactly from HEAD using git show piped to write - NOT git restore or git checkout - and then proved no authored text was lost by comparing the comment/code multiset, finding HEAD and the working copy shared the same 47 distinct comment lines with only copies differing. The root cause was then fixed by hoisting four lambdas out of the Dictionary literal into named locals, after which three consecutive passes were idempotent. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THAT ONE FILE: an agent under pressure who runs the formatter a second time to settle a diff can silently multiply a file, and because lint stays green and tests stay green there is no signal at all. The detection rule that would have caught it is the one already learned the hard way this session - a second pass that disagrees with the first is evidence, not noise. WORTH AN UPSTREAM REPORT to gdformat, and worth a tools-side guard later: fmt could hash the file before and after and fail loudly when one pass increases total bytes by a large factor. NOT FIXED in tooling here, only in the one file.

title: A nav button could be visible, enabled and dead at the same time, and nothing reported it
source: found 2026-10-03 while adding the missing button-press proof in a77e33d4
next: RESOLVED in a77e33d4, recorded for the trace rather than as open work. NavBar._on_slot_pressed read the route id from _routes, a render cache only _publish_routes fills, and _publish_routes only runs from _ready. title: The {} summary sentinel is overloaded: a screen bound with nothing supplied is indistinguishable from a screen with no actor
source: orchestrator, by driving all 16 routed screens 2026-10-03
next: THE {} SUMMARY SENTINEL IS OVERLOADED, so a screen that is bound but has nothing supplied reports IDENTICALLY to a screen with no actor at all. Found by driving all 16 routed screens rather than reading them. WHAT I MEASURED: 16 screens are routed in game/src/app/screen_routes.gd. Driving each with --path body --fresh --cmd refresh, 12 returned a populated summary (loot_encounter 38 keys, nation 26, body_cultivation_panel 24, sect 24, mind on its own path 25, qi on its own path 20, tribulation 20, destiny 19, technique_loadout 18, technique_codex 16, item_workbench 15, character 10, crafting 10, world_map 7) and 4 returned {}. I CHECKED MY OWN INSTRUMENT FIRST and was wrong twice. qi_cultivation_screen and mind_cultivation_screen bind perfectly on --path qi and --path mind respectively (20 and 25 keys) - I had driven all sixteen with --path body, so those two were my error. set_bonus_screen and socket_forge are different: BOTH extend UiScreen and therefore INHERIT setup(actor), which is exactly the inheritance trap this session has already cost two false alarms. The composition root binds them with extra shapes my driver does not perform - item_workbench_app.gd:301-306 does screen.call(setup, _actor) AND screen.call(apply_snapshot, SetBonusApi.inspect(_actor)) for ROUTE_SET_BONUS, and :280-282 does screen.call(setup, _actor) AND _forge.bind(screen) for ROUTE_SOCKET, while socket_forge.gd additionally exposes bind_view(view: Dictionary). So all sixteen screens ARE bindable and the driver is the thing that cannot bind four of them. THE REAL FINDING IS UNDERNEATH THAT: the UI standard says summary() returns {} when there is NO ACTOR, and every screen honours that. But a screen that IS bound and has been handed no snapshot also returns {}, because it has nothing to render. Those are different states - not enrolled, versus enrolled with nothing to show - and they render identically, so neither a player nor a headless test can tell them apart. That is the same class as the mind anchor gate reading open when it should read shut, and the same class as a refusal rendering like an offer: a state that is invisible because it is indistinguishable from another. Three questions nobody has decided, which is why this is filed rather than fixed: (1) should the {} sentinel be reserved strictly for no-actor, with a bound-but-empty screen reporting a distinct shape such as bound:true with an empty row list? (2) is apply_snapshot the right seam at all, or should a set-bonus screen read its snapshot through the facade like every other screen reads its state? (3) does the same overload affect any OTHER screen that renders from a pushed-in view rather than from the actor - socket forge and the workbench both qualify, and the workbench summary returned 15 keys so it is probably fine, but nobody has checked systematically. FIX FOR MY OWN INSTRUMENT, which I will do: game/tools/ui_driver.gd needs to perform the same three extra binding shapes the composition root performs, so a screen is driven exactly as the game drives it. A driver that binds a subset of what production binds will keep reporting live features as dead - which is how BL-0320 was filed against the loot screen when the fault was the harness.

title: The whole program gate is blocked by 8 ruff E501 lines in a live external agent files, and tools fmt structurally cannot clear them
next: THE ENTIRE PROGRAM GATE IS NOW BLOCKED BY EIGHT RUFF E501 FINDINGS IN TWO FILES OWNED BY A LIVE EXTERNAL AGENT - AND tools fmt STRUCTURALLY CANNOT CLEAR THEM. Measured 2026-10-03 by the orchestrator. WHERE THE GATE STANDS: fmt --check is CLEAN, 0 files to reformat. tools check therefore advances past stage one and now stops at stage two, lint, with exactly 8 findings: 6 in tools/map_assets.py (lines 77, 95, 113, 131, 317, 495) and 2 in tools/map_generate.py. gdlint is clean on BOTH game/src and game/tests. arch, deferred validate, backlog validate, data audit, cultivation validate, acquisition validate and realm_power check are ALL green. So eight long lines in one agent-s-live-files are the single remaining obstruction to uv run python -m tools check passing. THE TRAP, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THIS ENTRY: ruff format DELIBERATELY DOES NOT WRAP LONG STRING LITERALS. So no amount of running uv run python -m tools fmt will ever clear these eight, and an agent that trusts the formatter to fix the gate will conclude the gate is unfixable or will start editing the ruff configuration to make it pass - and loosening a lint threshold to clear a gate is masking, which is exactly what the acceptance criterion forbids. The only honest fixes are code changes in those two files: shorten the literal, split it with implicit string concatenation, or move the long help text into a form that wraps. THE OWNER IS ACTIVELY WORKING - this is not an abandoned file. tools/map_assets.py was modified at 17:02:13 and tools/map_generate.py at 16:45:30, and game/assets/world_map is taking new PNGs continuously - small_rock.png at 17:25:37, pool.png at 17:24:39, waterfall.png at 17:22:24 - so the files are being rewritten under me and their lint line numbers drift between runs. DO NOT RACE IT: editing a file another agent is actively rewriting is how this session destroyed uncommitted work six times. The correct action is to let the map work settle and then fix the eight literals. Whoever does it must re-run tools fmt --check afterwards, because a manual string split is exactly the shape that gdformat mishandles when a Dictionary literal is built from multi-line lambdas (BL-0364). RECORDED HONESTLY AND NOT MASKED, per the acceptance criterion: failures owned by concurrent agents are recorded, never hidden.

title: tools check can never reach green: ruff format cannot fix the long string literals that ruff check rejects as E501
source: measured tools lint exit 1 with 8 E501, plus a temp-file proof that uff format leaves a 127-char string at 127 while uff check reports E501 (127 > 100); session 2026-10-03
next: STRUCTURAL GATE FLAW, not 8 typos. tools check runs `fmt --check -> lint` in that order. tools/fmt.py:50 runs `ruff format`, and tools/lint.py:32 runs `ruff check tools`. pyproject.toml sets [tool.ruff] line-length = 100. `ruff format` will NOT split a string literal, but `ruff check` still reports E501 on it, so there exist lines that fmt provably cannot fix and lint provably rejects -- which means `tools check` is STRUCTURALLY UNABLE TO REACH GREEN while any string in tools/ exceeds 100 chars. PROOF: wrote a single 127-char string literal to a temp file, ran `uv run ruff format`, then `uv run ruff check --select E501`; the format pass left it at 127 and the check reported `E501 Line too long (127 > 100)`. MEASURED: tools lint exits 1 with 8 E501, all in tools/map_assets.py (lines 77, 95, 113, 131, 317, 495) and tools/map_generate.py (lines 289, 311); offending line lengths are 101-104 chars, just over the limit. The offenders are long descriptive prose (asset description strings) and one argparse help string. Both files were last committed 44 and 61 minutes ago by map-generation work, so they may still be in flight and are NOT this session's to wrap unilaterally. NOT FIXED HERE DELIBERATELY: the two available fixes are (a) wrap the 8 literals, which treats the symptom and will recur for the next author who writes a long description, and (b) raise line-length or ignore E501, which is loosening a threshold and needs argued justification plus a call from whoever owns the toolchain. The real fix is a decision about which rules the linter is allowed to enforce, not an edit to map_assets.py. NEXT: an owner decides whether tools/lint.py should run the formatter-compatible rule set (in which case E501 is dropped because the formatter already governs width) or whether long prose strings get wrapped by convention; then either the 8 lines are wrapped or the lint rule set changes, and the choice gets an ADR because it changes what the gate can ever say.

title: ADR 0062's anti-convergence claim is decorative: commonborn tops all three axes under the test's own metric, and the cap that permits it was invented in the test file
source: lineage program design audit 2026-10-03, independently recomputed from the .tres files
next: ADR 0062's load-bearing balance claim is that 'race x path is a partition, not a tier list' and that no race is best at everything. Recomputing the shipped content with the shipped metric (game/tests/modules/race/test_race_content.gd:194 _axis_strength) gives commonborn leading ALL THREE axes - QI 1.04, BODY 1.04, MIND 1.04 - because it closes mind (scored -1000), has no realm ceiling, carries a 36500-day lifespan and gives +1.0 to all seven base attributes, while the three specialists give 2-4 on one attribute and nothing elsewhere. commonborn is also the fallback every raceless actor is born into (ADR 0108: 'no actor is ever born raceless'), so the default body is the strongest body. TWO SEPARATE DEFECTS: (1) the threshold is a test-file invention - MAX_TOP_AXES := 2 at test_race_content.gd:19 - and grepping all 111 ADRs for 'top-2'/'two axes'/'more than one axis' finds zero hits, so the test asserts a rule no ADR states; (2) a metric that scores a closed path as -1000 cannot express a body plan, because 'leading an axis you are forbidden to enter' is an artifact of the scoring function rather than a balance property. THE FIX, and it is the one ADR 0062 actually cares about: delete the scoring metric and assert the STRUCTURAL claim instead - every authored race must be refused at least one breakthrough by ADR 0109's gate. That is what the partition means, it is already implemented, and it cannot be gamed by a constant. commonborn will still need a realm ceiling or a narrower affinity set, because as shipped the body everyone is born into is the widest, the longest-lived of the non-stoneborn, and the numerically best on all three axes. This is a content ruling as much as a test fix, so it wants the owner's judgement.

title: tools check short-circuits, so 8 committed E501 stop arch, the ledgers, the data audit, the tests and BOTH incident guards from ever running
source: measured tools lint exit 1 on committed code + tools check stage order from AGENTS.md; audit 2026-10-03 (compounds BL-0370, which is why 	ools fmt cannot clear them either)
next: GATE-ORDERING FRAGILITY, and the most serious finding of the 2026-10-03 audit. tools check runs its stages in order: fmt --check -> lint -> arch -> deferred validate -> backlog validate -> data audit -> test. Because it is a short-circuiting sequence, ANY early stage failing means every later stage never runs. MEASURED: tools lint exits 1 on 8 committed E501 in tools/map_assets.py and tools/map_generate.py (confirmed committed, not in-flight: `git status --short` on both is empty), so `tools check` halts at stage 2 and NEVER REACHES arch, the incident/backlog/deferred ledgers, the data audit, or the tests. That means the two incident guards -- test_no_unbounded_wait.gd (INC-0001 disk) and test_no_deferred_free.gd (INC-0002 memory) -- are not executed at all by the gate that is supposed to run them, purely because one agent left 8 long Python strings unformatted. COMPOUNDS BL-0370: those same 8 lines are exactly the class `ruff format` provably cannot fix, so running `tools fmt` does not clear them either. The hazard is therefore not one agent's untidy Python; it is that the safety guards sit DOWNSTREAM of a stage that unrelated routine work can red-flag, so a cosmetic failure silently disables every guard after it. SECOND, SAME SHAPE: arch_rules is itself RED on arrival, 2 pre-existing failures in test_arch_rules.gd because it asserts `tools arch` still warns about `src/app/consumable_system.gd` and that file no longer exists (game/src/app now holds 15 .gd files). The warning went quiet, which is exactly the 'a guard that stopped firing reads like a clean tree' failure mode that test's own comment warns about. NET: the gate cannot currently be used as a green/red signal at all, because two of its stages are red for reasons unrelated to what they gate. NEXT: decide whether the safety guards must run BEFORE the cosmetic stages rather than after them, since a guard that can be switched off by an unrelated lint error is not a guard. That is a change to the order in tools/check.py, so it needs an ADR.

concurrent agent. The reported line number pointed at a region that did not match the
file's real content at the same instant - the loader read a torn snapshot - and a
direct ast.parse of the same path succeeded minutes later with no edit in between.
Treat "every tools command is unavailable" as transient and re-verify the file parses
before reporting it as a defect. A structural fix would move the route table into its
own module so the loader's import graph is smaller, but that is a refactor with its
own risk and is not owed while agents are in flight.

title: A single mid-write file in tools/ takes the whole toolchain down, so a gate reading red during concurrent edits is not evidence of a defect
source: Measured 2026-10-03. tools/data.py was 45 lines mid-edit and tools/__main__ refused to load: 'unterminated string literal (line 889) ... every tools command is unavailable until it loads.' That killed fmt --check, lint, arch, data audit and every tracker write at once, while the SAME file parsed cleanly under a direct ast.parse microseconds later (the loader had read a stale snapshot). Two distinct false reds in one hour, both from reading a moving target: (1) tools test printing '433 passed, 0 failed' and exiting 1, which was a file written one second earlier plus, in a second instance, godot.lock contention from my own overlapping runs; (2) fmt reporting 6 files to reformat that agents were actively writing.
next: When a gate stage reads red while agents are in flight, check the file's mtime and parse it directly before believing the message. Never fix a moving file: reformatting or repairing it edits another agent's work mid-write. Wait for mtime to stabilise, then re-measure.

title: Deferring to a live agent is only sound when re-measured: a finished owner left the map gate blocked for hours
source:
Measured twice in one session, opposite outcomes. tools/map_assets.py had been
reported as "owned by a live external agent" for hours; checking git status showed
the file COMMITTED and CLEAN with no write for 90 minutes, and its last commit was
db4fc412. The agent had finished and left, so the deferral was protecting nothing.
Conversely game/src/modules/combat_engine/body_wounds.gd was genuinely dirty and
written 45 seconds before the same check. The two states look identical from the
conversation and only the filesystem distinguishes them.
next:
Never report a file as owned by a live agent from memory or from an earlier
measurement: re-check `git status --short -- <path>` and its mtime before deferring,
and say so with the timestamp. A deferral with no timestamp is indistinguishable from
a real blocker and silently stalls the gate. After fixing a file yourself, verify
which of the OTHER findings are genuinely live the same way rather than assuming the
first sample generalises.

title: The body ascent defect was the missing progress ROW, not missing wording: the unmet list always stated the gate
source:
The orchestrator reported the defect as "the player is owed an ascent and the screen
says nothing about it" and "renders no ascent wording". BOTH were overstated, and the
second body-ascent agent repeated them. Measured against the before-state: unmet[]
already carried "Walk the ascent: 4 of 4 steps to walk", so the player WAS told a gate
existed. What was missing was the ascent ROW - the progress bar and the "4/4" position.
The player was told a gate existed with no indication of how far along the walk they
were. Separately, the claim that the finished-walk branch was also dead is false:
outstanding == "" requires a completed AscensionState, which makes ascension_ok true,
which makes required false, so that branch never matched the first required test - its
assertion was PASSING AT BASELINE. Only the owed case was dead.
next:
Describe a rendering defect by what the node actually contained, not by what the screen
"failed to say". Read the before-drive output verbatim: unmet[] is rendered text too.
When reporting a dead branch, check whether the predicate can reach it before calling it
unreachable - a branch whose assertion passes at baseline was never the defect.

title: The body ascent defect was a missing ROW, not a missing requirement: the sentence was already on screen inside unmet
source:
I briefed both body-ascent agents that "the player is owed an ascent and the screen says
nothing about it". That was false. The before-drive already carried "Walk the ascent: 4 of
4 steps to walk" inside the `unmet` list: the requirement sentence WAS on screen. What was
missing was the ascent ROW - the bar and the player's position in the walk. A player was told
a gate existed, with no progress toward it and nothing stating how far they had come. The
correct defect statement is "no row", not "no wording", and the fix is keyed on `outstanding`
alone so the row can exist.
next:
When briefing a defect from a summary, verify the rendered node AND the read model before
stating what is missing; a populated field and a blank node are different defects with
different fixes. This agent measured it and corrected two of my claims: the `""` branch was
reachable (a completed AscensionState makes required false, so the test never matched) and its
assertion passed at baseline - only the owed case was dead.

title: At the terminal realm an unwalked ascent states a requirement beside a button that is never offered
source:
At the terminal realm an ascent that has not been walked yields required == false while
outstanding is still non-empty, so the screen states a live requirement beside a control
that is not offered. Reached through normal play only if reaching R30 stops requiring
is_complete(); currently unreachable because R30 requires it, and reachable only through
a doctored save. The two halves disagree in body_cultivation/api.gd's required and in
core's ascension_ok terminal exemption, so neither could be fixed from the ui/ files that
owned the row. This is the same "requirement with no affordance" shape that 39b148ef
raised for the NO_ASCENT case.
next:
Decide which of the two owns the terminal exemption: if the walk is genuinely owed at the
terminal realm, ascension_ok must keep required true; if it is genuinely waived, the row
must stop stating it. The split is deliberate in neither place, so one of them is wrong.
Reachable-by-doctored-save does not mean unreachable, and a save editor is not the threat
model here - a player who completes the ladder by an unintended route is.

title: The acquisition count fell 4132 to 1553 because HEAD counted every craft-only item as a delivered root, not because craft stopped working
source: tools data audit on one unchanged tree: 7981/7982 obtainable in the content graph, 1553/7982 deliverable by shipping code, exit 0. HEAD (9b26fc45) reports 4132 for the same tree. Cause, measured by loading HEAD and the working tree side by side: HEAD _runtime_roots does 'if kind == craft: continue', which leaves source_type None, so an item whose ONLY source is craft: lands in roots outright and its recipe never has to close. 2791 craft-only items were counted that way and only 216 are reachable through the recipe closure; the other ~2575 rest on inputs no shipping route delivers. HEAD also contradicted its own _obtainable, which deliberately excludes craft from root_types. Roots 4087 vs 1296, reachable 4132 vs 1553. tools/data.py is being edited concurrently (sha changed twice inside one 60s poll), so this fix is uncommitted in-flight work by another agent.
next: When a measurement moves, diff the two implementations rather than reasoning about the delta: importing HEAD and the working tree in one process and comparing roots/reachable named the craft branch in a single run. Never commit a file another agent is actively writing - hash it twice 10s apart first.
