title: A parse error in another agent's in-flight nation/api.gd stops the whole app loading, so every suite that mounts ItemWorkbenchApp reports a false green
source: game/src/modules/nation/api.gd does not parse, so item_workbench_app.gd does not load and no suite that mounts the app can execute. Two successive causes, both in that one file: first NationState.R_NOT_A_POLITY (referenced at api.gd:583; nation_state.gd declares R_NOT_A_PARTY and no R_NOT_A_POLITY), then - still open at 20:43, 30 minutes after their last edit - institution_resolver.gd:98 calls NationApi.act(actor, periods, tier) and no static func act exists. The shape is the dangerous one: SeamHarness._boot() returns early on boot_error, so tools test --suite test_item_pipeline printed "80 passed, 0 failed" while the whole walk never ran. A green that skipped the claim is what AGENTS.md calls a dead seam, and the passed count is not the test count.
next: CLOSED BY COMMIT 24afa44f, and the mechanism is now prevented rather than merely noted. The defect was that the runner tallied assertions and never checked that a test ran, so a body returning early on a failed harness recorded neither a pass nor a failure and the suite printed 0 passed / 0 failed with exit 0. The runner now counts assertions either side of each test call and fails any test that makes none, naming it. Proven both ways rather than asserted: a throwaway suite pairing an early-returning test with a real one reports 1 passed / 1 failed and exits 1, and the six arch_rules suites report 3028 passed with zero vacuous reports, so the guard stays inert on healthy tests. The Results line format is unchanged on purpose, because tools/test.py keys on that literal prefix to tell a completed run from a runner that died. WORTH KEEPING IN MIND when reading any tally from this repo: a suite that fails to LOAD now reports its load failure honestly, so a green really does mean tests executed.

title: GUARDS: mind suites dereference the result of MindAdvancement.start without a null guard, so a fixture failure becomes a runtime error that reports green and skips every later suite
source: Found by mutation on 2026-10-03: with api.train_channel stubbed to refuse, test_breakthrough_attempt.gd:218-225 raises Invalid access to property or key attempt_id on a base object of type Nil. assert_ne(started, null) at :220 reports the failure but does not stop the test, so the dereference still runs and the runner dies mid-suite - tools/test.py then reports the run as incomplete and every suite after the abort is skipped while reporting nothing. This is the documented failure mode in tools/test.py: a GDScript runtime error aborts the function and the caller continues, so a test can look finished.

Until then, a red mind run means two different things - an assertion failure or a crashed fixture - and only the exit code and the stderr tail tell them apart.

title: A Variant-inference parse error in modules/nation/api.gd takes down the whole gate, tools boot included
source: root 2026-10-03, found while extending the boot probe
next: REPORTED, NOT FIXED - modules/nation is another agent's in-flight lane (the file is modified and uncommitted). res://src/modules/nation/api.gd:591 reads 'var def := catalog.office_definitions(NationState.nation_id(ledger)).get(String(office_id), null)'. Dictionary.get returns Variant, so := infers Variant and Godot treats the inference warning as an error. The consequence is much wider than the one file: every script that transitively depends on it fails to compile, so 'Failed to compile depended scripts' cascades and res://tools/boot_probe.gd cannot load the main scene at all. That takes down the tools boot GATE STEP, which is the only check that proves the game starts and that a fight mints a reward. Observed cascade: nation/api.gd:591, then event/event_prize.gd, then boot_probe.gd:67 on load(). Note tools lint reported 8 GDScript findings earlier in other files and did NOT name this one, so the lint stage does not currently see compile-time inference errors in a dependency chain. SUGGESTED FIX for whoever owns the lane: give def an explicit type rather than inferring it from .get(), e.g. 'var def: Variant = ...' or hoist the .get() result into a typed local.

title: Two agents mid-refactor at once means the app layer does not compile, so tools boot and every tests/app suite are unevaluable
source: root 2026-10-03, measured across two consecutive checks
next: STRUCTURAL FINDING, not a defect in any one file. Measured state: module-level suites are fine (uv run python -m tools test --suite modules/items reports 2159 passed, 0 failed, 15 suites) because a scoped suite loads only its own dependency chain. But anything that mounts the composition root is broken, by TWO independent in-flight edits at once: (1) game/src/app/institution_resolver.gd is UNTRACKED and calls NationApi.act() at line 98, which does not exist - Parse Error: Static function act() not found in base NationApi, cascading through world_pulse.gd and item_workbench_app.gd so the main scene cannot load and tools boot is red; (2) game/src/modules/sect/ is mid-refactor (api.gd, sect_def.gd and sect_state.gd modified, sect_act.gd new and untracked), leaving 'Could not resolve class SectReadModel', which fails every tests/app suite. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE GATE: a gate can only be evaluated at a moment when no agent is mid-edit. With several agents working concurrently, 'tools check is green' is not a steady state, it is a snapshot. Anyone reading a red gate should first run a scoped module suite to distinguish 'this is broken' from 'a peer is mid-write' - that distinction costs one command and prevents chasing a defect that is not theirs. No fix proposed here because both files belong to peers who are actively in them; editing either risks a write-write conflict, which is worse than the wait (INC-0003).

title: A git index.lock held by live agents blocks commits indefinitely, and removing it corrupts their work rather than unblocking mine
source: Measured 2026-10-03. Six to seven live git processes were committing continuously; the lock reappeared within 60 s of clearing. Two commit attempts failed with 'Unable to create index.lock'. A blanket instruction to 'remove the lock if git crashed' is the standard advice and it is WRONG here: with ~20 concurrent agents, a lock that reappears in under a minute belongs to a live process, and deleting it lets two git processes write one index. HEAD was visibly advancing between attempts (7d5601cc, ba53b3b0, d691e874, 821f71a6).
next: Never remove .git/index.lock in this repo. Check for live git processes and whether HEAD is moving; if so, wait and retry, and leave the work uncommitted rather than force it - uncommitted is recoverable by the next committer, a corrupted index is not. Commit opportunistically between bursts rather than retrying in a loop.

title: sect_read_model.gd does not parse, so SectReadModel is unresolvable and every tests/app suite plus tools boot fail to load
source: root 2026-10-03, bisected from the boot probe through a scoped sect run
next: REAL DIAGNOSIS NOW KNOWN - replaces the earlier guess. The file parses as far as the engine is concerned, but the tail of static func summary is SEMANTICALLY INTERLEAVED, not merely mis-indented. REAL ERROR from Godot own parser is: Parse Error - Expected indented block after for block. HOW TO GET IT, since a scene run only reports the useless 'because of a parser error': run the script alone with --check-only, i.e. via tools/godot.py the runner with --headless --path game --check-only -s res://src/modules/sect/sect_read_model.gd. That prints the actual message. EXTENT: six block headers sit at indent 1 with their bodies at the same indent - lines 230, 236, 249, 253, 257 and 259. THE IMPORTANT WARNING: do NOT just add indentation. Line 231 reads var sworn := catalog.sect_definition(sect_id) INSIDE a loop that iterates doctrine_id, and sect_id is not a parameter or in-scope variable of summary(ledger, catalog) - the params are ledger and catalog. Lines 230 to 234 therefore appear to be fragments belonging to a different function, interleaved into summary by a bad edit. De-indenting alone would turn a parse error into an undefined-variable read and silently wrong output, which is worse than not compiling. REBUILDING THE INTENDED CONTROL FLOW IS THE OWNER DECISION, because it requires knowing which statements belong in summary and which belong in a helper - that is design, not repair. STATE: the file is COMMITTED and modules/sect is clean in git, so HEAD ITSELF DOES NOT PARSE. Every tests/app suite and the tools boot GATE STEP fail to load; the scoped discriminator still holds - uv run python -m tools test --suite modules/sect RUNS rather than failing to load. MEASUREMENT NOTE for whoever greps: a private probe that greps stderr for the string Parse Error on a -s boot_probe.gd run reported COMPILE_OK and was WRONG - the same tree failed the authoritative tools boot. Trust tools boot and its log file under build/logs, not a grep over one script run.

title: Nothing in production calls attach_sea, so every actor the game builds has no Sea of Consciousness and the whole Mind path is inert in play
source: measured 2026-10-03: attach_sea has 1 reference in res://src (its own definition) and 0 callers; app/actor_factory.gd:102-107 with_mind_cultivation never calls it; all 38 call sites are in tests/ and ui_driver.gd. Cap verified: MAX_FACADE_PUBLIC_METHODS=12 (rules.py:134) and mind sits at exactly 12. ADR 0095 precedent. Agent ses_efe1c0633ffeVPxQFOwNGhRrJM
next: THE MIND PATH IS INERT IN PLAY. Nothing in res://src calls MindCultivationApi.attach_sea -- measured: attach_sea has exactly ONE reference under game/src, its own definition at api.gd:38, and ZERO callers. The single production enrolment path, app/actor_factory.gd:102-107 with_mind_cultivation, calls MindCultivationApi.attach(actor) then MindTraining.synchronize(actor) and never attach_sea. The sea is created in only two places in the whole codebase: api.gd:44 inside attach_sea, and core/actor.gd:413 on save restore (v3+). CONSEQUENCE, and this is the whole point: an actor the game builds has no Sea of Consciousness, so MindTraining.cultivate refuses at training.gd:56-57, MindTraining.recover refuses at training.gd:125-126 because it requires MindCultivationApi.sea(actor) != null, and MindCultivationApi.summary reports mind_power 0.0 and turbulence 0.0. Every Mind mechanic is unreachable in the shipped game. WHY 10,186 GREEN ASSERTIONS NEVER CAUGHT IT: all 38 attach_sea call sites are in game/tests/ and game/tools/ui_driver.gd:258. Every hand-built test actor attaches the sea explicitly, so the fixture supplies exactly what production withholds. This is ADR 0095 defect class (2) verbatim -- for qi the same shape read "the whole qi path was inert in play while every test, having built its actor by hand, passed", and ADR 0095 fixed it by folding the attachment INTO attach, because the composition root's single call must leave the actor ready. THE FIX IS THE SAME ONE LINE: have MindCultivationApi.attach call attach_sea(actor). It also HARDENS the cap fix, because attach_sea then has a production caller and can never be a candidate for the MindAccess move; path_def (zero production callers, test_mind_path.gd:26 only) remains the only safe thing to relocate. SECOND CONSTRAINT ON THE SAME FIX, verified: tools/arch/rules.py:134 MAX_FACADE_PUBLIC_METHODS = 12 and MindCultivationApi is at exactly 12 public methods today (attach, path_def, sea, attach_sea, summary, preview, cultivate, meditate, train_channel, strengthen_sea, strengthen_anchor, try_breakthrough), so adding recover_next on its own is a hard tools/arch failure AND a hard test_ui_conventions.gd:173-189 failure. The facade must shed a slot first, by ADR 0095's exact pattern -- move path_def into a new game/src/modules/mind_cultivation/access.gd as `class_name MindAccess`, which the facade counter never sees. NET 12 -> 11 -> 12. Also note the cap is far more widely hit than AGENTS.md records: 17 of 37 module facades sit at exactly 12 (bloodline, body_cultivation, clan, custody, destiny, domain, holdings, items, loot, market, mind_cultivation, npc, sect, set_bonus, soul, techniques, world), while AGENTS.md names only items and body_cultivation. That sentence is stale and should stop being the thing an agent trusts. RELATED LEDGER CONFLICT, resolved in favour of DEF-0076: BL-0107's next says "Add recover_next to api.gd" and does not mention the cap at all, which cannot work; DEF-0076:76 says "The mind facade is at the 12-method cap so SPLIT it rather than grow it", which is correct. Both also cite stale line numbers. A THIRD, SEPARATE PROBLEM that does not block the fix: DEF-0188 records that all 30 mind recovery elixirs are unacquirable (their reagents declare only gather: and quest: sources and ItemSources.KINDS marks both shipped: false), so wiring recover_next changes "30 dead elixirs" into "30 elixirs no player can obtain" unless DEF-0188 lands too. NEXT: one agent, one job -- fold attach_sea into attach, move path_def to MindAccess, add recover_next, update test_mind_path.gd:26, and add the facade-level recovery tests to test_mind_recovery.gd reusing its existing _actor/_stock/_recovery_id helpers with NO new fixture. Mutation-proof the consumption claim by making training.gd:136 `if true: # MUTATION-BL0107-CONSUME` on a throwaway copy: the wound still closes and recover_next still returns true, so only the elixir-count assertion can catch it. Then close DEF-0076 naming that guard and correct BL-0107's next to DEF-0076's wording.

title: HEAD has a committed mutation probe: breakthrough_condition.gd in HEAD is missing the progress gate entirely
source: measured 2026-10-03 against HEAD:game/src/modules/mind_cultivation/breakthrough_condition.gd; escalated by the agent that found it. Working tree is correct, HEAD is not. Caused by assigning one file to two agents in the same wave
next: HEAD IS CURRENTLY CORRUPT AND THIS IS A LIVE INSTANCE, not a historical one. Measured 2026-10-03 against HEAD:game/src/modules/mind_cultivation/breakthrough_condition.gd: the conjunction is missing its FIRST TERM. HEAD reads `return ( # MUTATION-BL0161-1` followed immediately by `actor.stats.derived(Stat.COMPREHENSION) >= target_seed.comprehension_required` -- state.progress >= target_seed.progress_required is GONE, and one MUTATION marker is committed inside res://src. So every clone, and anyone who checks HEAD out, gets a Mind breakthrough with NO progress gate at all. This is BL-0161's own mutation probe, committed while it was applied. WHY IT IS STILL TRUE DESPITE FIXES: the working tree is CORRECT -- both progress_required and comprehension_required are present there -- because the owning agent restored the progress term by hand. The divergence between working tree and HEAD is the dangerous shape: everyone currently working sees a correct gate, so nothing looks wrong, while HEAD stays broken until the file is committed clean. NOT COMMITTED AS A FIX, DELIBERATELY: the working tree currently carries a SECOND live probe from the other agent working that file -- the sea-fill line `and sea.ratio(actor) >= target_seed.sea_fill_required` is presently replaced by `# MUTATION-BL0161-5` -- so committing the file right now would trade a missing progress gate in HEAD for a missing sea-fill gate in HEAD. The correct resolution is to let the in-flight proof finish, restore the probe, then commit the file with all ten terms, and confirm with a grep that HEAD contains progress_required and zero MUTATION markers. ROOT CAUSE IS A CONTROLLER ERROR, and it is worth recording as such: breakthrough_condition.gd was assigned to TWO agents in the same wave. One was migrating the ADR 0109 race gate, the other was building per-term observability tests for BL-0161. Neither was at fault; both followed their briefs, and they ping-ponged the same file until one escalated. A disjoint-file split that overlaps by one file is not a disjoint split. NEXT: one owner for breakthrough_condition.gd until it is committed clean, then a verification step that greps HEAD for MUTATION markers in res://src, because the stranded-mutation guard scans the WORKING TREE ONLY and by construction cannot see this -- which is exactly what INC-0007 says and this instance proves.

title: ui/screens/destiny_screen.gd violates the facade rule because DestinyApi is at its 12-method cap and never publishes the event bus
source: Measured 2026-10-03 with tools arch: 'src/ui/screens/destiny_screen.gd:269: ui/ may reference destiny only through modules/destiny/api.gd'. The screen calls DestinyProjection.events() at :269 to connect fate_earned and destiny_earned (:270-273). DestinyProjection.events() exists (destiny_projection.gd:131) and the facade USES it internally (api.gd:182, :342) but never re-exports it, so ui/ has no legal way to reach the bus at all. This is an interface gap rather than a typo: the fix is to publish events() on the facade, and DestinyApi is at exactly 12 public methods, which is rules.MAX_FACADE_PUBLIC_METHODS - a 13th FAILS tools arch. The file has been idle over 70 minutes, so this is not an in-flight write.
next: Decide deliberately between three options and record why: (a) publish events() as a 13th facade method and raise MAX_FACADE_PUBLIC_METHODS, which weakens a rule other facades sit exactly at; (b) fold the two signal subscriptions behind an existing facade method so the count does not move - the screen only needs to know a fate or destiny was earned, so a facade that already publishes a summary may be able to carry it; (c) move the screen's reactivity to summary() polling, consistent with the rule that ui/ renders state rather than subscribing to module internals. (b) is the one worth trying first and is the only one that does not touch a shared cap. Whoever fixes it must also confirm the is_connected() guards at :270-273 survive, since a reconnected screen otherwise fires one handler per press.

Treat the remaining eight as the real board. The lesson worth keeping is that a standing defect list decays silently - nothing in tools check fails when one of its entries becomes untrue, so a list carried across turns needs a re-measure before it is dispatched against, exactly as a stale test does.

title: Three test_ui_conventions guards assert only inside a filtered loop, so they enforce nothing when nothing matches -- including the ui/ may-not-reach-past-a-facade rule
source: measured 2026-10-03: all three report 'asserted nothing'; game/src/ui holds 52 .gd and 46 .tscn so UI_ROOT and the walker are fine; the shape is the cause. Includes the ui/ facade isolation guard
next: THREE UI GUARD TESTS ARE VACUOUS BY CONSTRUCTION, and one of them is the guard that keeps ui/ from reaching past a module facade. Measured 2026-10-03 on game/tests/ui/test_ui_conventions.gd, which reports `asserted nothing` for all three. MECHANISM: each puts its assert_eq INSIDE a filtered loop, so when nothing matches the filter the body never runs and the test makes ZERO assertions. game/src/ui is not empty -- 52 .gd and 46 .tscn files -- and UI_ROOT is `res://src/ui` (line 17) with a correct recursive walker at :431-451, so this is not a broken path. It is the shape. The three: (1) test_no_ui_file_reaches_a_module_by_anything_but_its_facade at :197 asserts only inside `for module_dir in _module_dirs()` and only for .tscn files, so it says nothing unless some scene instances a module file directly -- and that is EXACTLY the rule that keeps a module's internals out of the UI, so a green run of it proves less than it appears to. (2) test_no_ui_script_uses_onready at :255 asserts per .gd file and should therefore assert ~52 times, so its zero count needs explaining before anyone trusts it; the loop shape alone does not account for it and the real cause is still open. (3) test_ui_scripts_resolve_their_nodes_lazily at :273 skips any file that does not call get_node_or_null, so it is silent on every panel that resolves nothing. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A RED TEST: the test framework reports zero assertions as a FAILURE, which is the right call and stops the rot from being silent -- but the same shape means these guards would have passed unnoticed while enforcing nothing, which is the failure mode test_arch_rules.gd just had (its app/ stateful-system check went quiet because the offender was correctly deleted) and the mode test_no_stranded_mutation.gd addresses by self-hosting a liveness case. NONE OF THIS IS MIND WORK and none of it was touched here. NOT FIXED HERE ON PURPOSE: game/tests/ui is not owned by this session and the file is large and shared. THE FIX IS A LIVENESS TERM, NOT A LOOP CHANGE: each of the three needs a case that asserts unconditionally on a synthetic fixture, the way test_arch_rules.gd's rewrite now asserts that app/ ships a stateful system so its correspondence check cannot pass vacuously, and the way test_no_stranded_mutation.gd holds test_the_guard_does_not_flag_its_own_source. A guard whose only assertions live inside a filter is a guard that can be switched off by the absence of the thing it watches. NEXT: the owner of game/tests/ui adds one unconditional assertion per guard -- for (1) a synthetic scene that DOES instance a module file and must be rejected, for (2) a synthetic script containing @onready that must be caught, for (3) a synthetic panel that resolves nodes without _bind_nodes() -- and each is proved load-bearing by mutation. Until then treat the ui/ facade isolation rule as unguarded.

title: A newborn is built with bare Actor.new(), so it never gets attach_core_resources() - the child has no health or stamina pool and cannot be damaged or healed
source: lineage program agent audit 2026-10-03 (bg-3-d88dcb86), independently verified by reading fertility/api.gd:147 against actor_factory.gd:12
next: CONFIRMED, and it is the orchestrator's own bug rather than a found gap. FertilityApi.resolve_offspring does `var child := Actor.new(...)` at game/src/modules/fertility/api.gd:147 and then attaches ONLY race and bloodline. It never goes through ActorFactory.build, which is where game/src/app/actor_factory.gd:12 calls actor.attach_core_resources() - the pools every actor carries, with capacities derived from stats (ADR 0025). ActorFactory's own docstring at :186-188 states the rule this breaks: 'Every inhabitant of this game is an Actor ... so this builds through build() and gets the SAME provider spine the player gets' (ADR 0074). So a child born in play would have no health pool, no stamina pool, no sect ledger, no clan ledger and no element provider - it would be an actor that cannot be hurt. It is invisible to every existing test because test_fertility.gd builds children through the same path and never asserts a pool exists. WHY IT IS NOT FIXED HERE: fertility cannot name app/ - LAYER_DEPS makes app private (rules.py, PRIVATE_UNITS), so resolve_offspring cannot call ActorFactory directly. THE FIX IS AN INJECTED MINTER, and the repo already has the precedent twice: NpcApi.set_minter / DomainSpawner.set_minter (npc_boot.gd:29-40) exist precisely so a module can mint a complete actor without naming app/. Add the same seam to fertility - a settable actor builder, defaulting to the bare Actor.new path so headless tests still work, wired in ActorFactory so a real game gets a complete child. This is the same class as BL-0277 (no producer): it only bites once something actually conceives, which is why nothing has caught it.

title: A starting hero cannot obtain any wearable gear through the domain loop: every reachable fight pays consumables, tokens or above-tier drops
source: root 2026-10-03, boot probe equip phase, with a positive control proving the equip seam itself works
next: REPORTED, NOT FIXED - the content is not mine and the fix is a design decision about what the lowest tier pays. WHAT WAS MEASURED, in a real boot of the shipped main scene: the fight, the claim and the bag all work (pending drops 2 to 0, bag 3 to 5 rows, both rewards claimed), but of the drops claimed across four domains at the lowest authored tier, NONE can be worn: I50_earth_geyser_aged (category consumable, subcategory powder), Z27_immortal_augustinian_label (misc/token), E4_spirit_bullionoffice_clinker, artifact_iron_titan_ore (an artifact, which contends for the single artifact slot). THE POSITIVE CONTROL IS THE IMPORTANT HALF: the same run then walked every row the bag already held and the hero own Equip control ACCEPTED armor_iron_helm, so the equip button resolves, the action bar is wired, and pressing Equip equips. That rules out the alternative explanation - a probe whose Equip lookup is broken looks identical to a content gap, and that is exactly what this control exists to exclude. So the loop is wired and the CONTENT is what is short. WORTH KNOWING before anyone calls it a broken pipeline: wearable tier-1 equipment demonstrably exists in the corpus - 266 mortal-grade equipment items, being 42 armor, 41 weapon, 49 accessory, 18 greaves, 30 bandolier, 35 lens, 45 artifact and 6 orb. The gear is authored and ruled for a slot; the low-tier tables simply are not paying it out. RELATED: a second domain reported that the boss died and minted no reward at all, which is a separate refusal worth chasing. WHAT A FIX LOOKS LIKE: either the lowest authored tier tables roll from a pool that includes tier-1 wearable gear, or the starting hero tier is set so the tier it can fight also pays gear it may equip. What is NOT the fix: weakening the grade gate or the category refusal. Both are correct - the gate is refusing a consumable because it is a consumable.
